lead.headline: Institutional RWA Pivot Accelerates as TradFi Giants Enter Tokenization
lead.tldr: The week is defined by a strategic shift where traditional financial powerhouses are moving beyond simple custody into active tokenized asset issuance and prediction markets.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is our analysis of the critical shifts in institutional adoption and the escalating security risks facing the ecosystem this week.

top_signals.title: Capital B Gains Authority to Raise Up to $120B for Bitcoin
top_signals.summary: Capital B shareholders have authorized the company to raise up to $120 billion through equity and credit instruments. This massive financing capacity is specifically intended to fund the company's strategic acquisition of Bitcoin.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The scale of this authorization indicates a move toward 'corporate treasury' Bitcoin strategies on a sovereign-level magnitude.

top_signals.title: G7 Flags North Korean Cybercrime After $2B Stolen in 2025
top_signals.summary: G7 leaders have issued a warning regarding North Korean cybercrime following the theft of at least $2 billion in digital assets in 2025. The alert highlights the increasing scale and sophistication of DPRK-linked hacking operations targeting the crypto ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $2B theft underscores a systemic vulnerability in bridge and cross-chain security that remains the primary hurdle for institutional capital safety.

top_signals.title: Coinbase launching tokenized US stocks, backed 1:1, with holders able to receive dividends
top_signals.summary: Coinbase is launching tokenized US stocks that are backed 1:1 by the underlying assets. This initiative allows holders to receive dividends, positioning Coinbase against rivals like Robinhood and Kraken in the RWA space.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Coinbase's move into 1:1 tokenized stocks bridges the gap between equity markets and on-chain settlement, intensifying the RWA competition.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed a Record $6.4B in 30 Days
top_signals.summary: US Bitcoin ETFs experienced a record $6.4 billion in outflows over a 30-day period. This trend coincides with a 17% drop in Bitcoin's price, suggesting a potential decline in institutional appetite.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Record ETF outflows suggest a short-term decoupling of institutional sentiment from the long-term bullish narrative.

top_signals.title: Charles Schwab to enter prediction markets with S&P 500 wagers: WSJ13m
top_signals.summary: Financial giant Charles Schwab is reportedly planning to enter the prediction markets space by offering wagers on the S&P 500. This move signals a growing institutional interest in the mechanisms of prediction markets, which are heavily utilized in the Web3 ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Charles Schwab's entry into prediction markets validates the utility of these mechanisms for hedging and price discovery at the highest institutional levels.

deals.summary: Capital B shareholders have authorized the company to raise up to $120 billion through equity and credit instruments. This massive financing capacity is specifically intended to fund the company's strategic acquisition of Bitcoin.

Prediction market platform Kalshi is reportedly in early discussions with investment banks regarding an initial public offering. This follows a massive $1 billion Series F funding round in May that valued the company at $22 billion.

MANTRA is being acquired by its previous backer, Inveniam, following a period of instability. The acquisition follows a major collapse of MANTRA's token value in 2025, leading to company restructuring and layoffs.

on_the_radar.title: Base targets June 25 mainnet launch for Beryl upgrade and new B20 token standard
on_the_radar.summary: Base is set to launch the Beryl upgrade on its mainnet on June 25. This update introduces the B20 native token standard and significantly reduces withdrawal delays to five days.

on_the_radar.title: CFTC, SEC request public comment to clarify definition of 'swaps' amid CME lawsuit
on_the_radar.summary: The CFTC and SEC are seeking public comments to clarify the definition of 'swaps' following a lawsuit from CME Group. The legal dispute centers on whether perpetual futures should be classified as futures contracts or swaps.

on_the_radar.title: Morgan Stanley files amendments for ETH and SOL ETFs, revealing lowest fees in market
on_the_radar.summary: Morgan Stanley has filed amendments for its proposed Ethereum and Solana ETFs, signaling active progress with the SEC. The filings reveal a strategy to offer the lowest fees in the market to attract investors.

on_the_radar.title: Celsius’ Mashinsky gets permanent trading ban in CFTC settlement
on_the_radar.summary: Alex Mashinsky, the founder of Celsius, has reached a settlement with the CFTC resulting in a permanent trading ban. This legal action follows the collapse of the Celsius lending platform and subsequent allegations of fraud.

on_the_radar.title: Fidelity launches GENIUS-aligned money market fund for stablecoin issuers
on_the_radar.summary: Fidelity has launched a money market fund specifically designed for stablecoin issuers to manage their reserve assets. This move bridges traditional finance and Web3 by providing institutional-grade liquidity management for the stablecoin ecosystem.

on_the_radar.title: Malta proposes DeFi rulebook covering DAOs under MiCA-era framework
on_the_radar.summary: Malta has proposed a new regulatory rulebook for DeFi and DAOs to align with the EU's MiCA framework. The move aims to provide legal clarity for decentralized governance and financial services within the jurisdiction.

on_the_radar.title: US regulators push user ID requirements for stablecoin issuers akin to regulated banks
on_the_radar.summary: US regulators are advocating for stablecoin issuers to implement user identification requirements similar to those mandated for traditional regulated banks. This move aims to align digital asset stability with existing financial compliance standards to mitigate risks.

on_the_radar.title: CME sues US derivatives regulator over crypto contract approval
on_the_radar.summary: CME is suing a US derivatives regulator over the approval of 'perpetual' crypto futures contracts for Kalshi. The exchange operator argues that this allowance violates existing laws.

linkedin_post:
The divide between TradFi and Web3 is blurring, but the transition is uneven. While Coinbase and Charles Schwab are aggressively integrating tokenized stocks and prediction markets—bringing legitimate utility to RWAs—the ecosystem is simultaneously battling a $2B drain from sophisticated state-sponsored cybercrime. 

We are seeing a paradox: institutional appetite for the 'mechanics' of crypto (tokenization, prediction markets) is growing, even as institutional 'sentiment' (ETF outflows) fluctuates. The winners of the next cycle won't just be those with the best tokens, but those who can provide the security infrastructure necessary to protect these massive inflows of capital.

Is the industry prioritizing product expansion over the fundamental security upgrades needed to sustain institutional trust?
